papers.title_in_file: How Much Structure Is Needed for Huge Quantum Speedups?
papers.what_it_is: An edited transcript of a Solvay Conference survey talk on which problems admit exponential quantum speedups.

assertions.value: The author states that many hopes for broad exponential quantum machine learning speedups have been killed, in part by Ewin Tang's work and later work that dequantized many quantum machine learning algorithms, in the sense that classical algorithms were found that were only polynomially slower than the quantum ones.
quotes: many of those hopes have been killed, in part by a breakthrough four years ago by Ewin Tang [42]
people found classical algorithms that were only polynomially slower than the quantum ones.
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey author's account of results by other authors, not proved in this paper.

assertions.value: The author reports that Yamakawa and Zhandry proved there is a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for their task with an appropriate error-correcting code, and that if f is a truly random function any classical algorithm would need exponentially many queries to f.
quotes: There is a polynomial-time quantum algorithm to solve this problem, for an appropriate
if f is a truly random function, then any classical algorithm would need exponentially many queries to f to solve the problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to Yamakawa and Zhandry.

assertions.value: The author states that in the circuit model, while nontrivial quantum algorithms are known, there is almost never any understanding of whether those algorithms are optimal, and reasonable lower bounds on gate counts can almost never be proved.
quotes: we almost never have any understanding of whether those algorithms are optimal.
we can almost never prove reasonable lower bounds
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's statement about the state of the field; no proof in the paper.

assertions.value: The author states that, given the huge overheads required for quantum error-correction, it will be a long time (if ever) before a quantum algorithm with a quadratic speedup yields a net win over classical computing in practice.
quotes: given the huge overheads required for quantum error-correction, it will be a long, long time (if ever) before a quantum algorithm with a quadratic speedup would yield a net win over classical computing in practice.
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's judgment, supported by a cited estimate.

papers.what_it_is: A simulation study that applies quantum autoencoders to image classification and compares them with classical models and a QCNN.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments assume an ideal situation in which quantum circuits yield perfect results, using a numerical simulator of quantum circuit measurements with noise-free conditions and a statevector simulator.
quotes: An ideal situation in which quantum circuits yield perfect results is assumed, and a numerical simulator of quantum circuit measurements is used.
Specifically, noise-free conditions are considered, and simulations are performed using a statevector simulator to model the
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors report that QAE classification reduces the number of trainable parameters by 98.0% compared with an FCNN with 0% sparsity and by 92.4% compared with NBMF with 74% sparsity, while its average accuracy is 9.2 and 13.9% lower than NBMF and FCNN, respectively.
quotes: 98.0% compared to FCNN with 0% sparsity
92.4% compared to NBMF with 74% sparsity
Despite this significant parameter reduction, QAE classification maintains 9.2 and 13.9% average accuracy reductions compared to NBMF and FCNN, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the eight-class MNIST task the test accuracy decreases significantly compared with four classes, and that raising the number of repetitions, the training data or the image size improved accuracy without reaching the four-class level.
quotes: As expected, the test accuracy decreases significantly.
however, the accuracy did not reach the level achieved in the four-class classification task.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulation study; figures are in Table 5, not in the quotes.

assertions.value: The authors report that, under identical training and testing data conditions, QCNN performance shows little to no significant improvement over the classical CNN.
quotes: under identical training and testing data conditions.
its performance shows little to no significant improvement over the classical CNN.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulation study.

papers.title_in_file: Parameterized quantum circuits as universal generative models for continuous multivariate distributions
papers.version_note: The file name carries the arXiv v1 style title (Expressivity of parameterized quantum circuits for generative modeling of ...); the text inside is v2 with the title Parameterized quantum circuits as universal generative models for continuous multivariate distributions. Same arXiv id 2402.09848.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that proves universality and resource bounds for expectation value sampling generative models built on parameterized quantum circuits.

assertions.value: The authors prove that expectation value samplers based on parameterized quantum circuits are universal generative models for multivariate distributions, with constructive proofs for two extremal circuit designs.
quotes: We prove the universality of such variational quantum algorithms for the generation of multivariate distributions.
The first central result of this work is that expectation value samplers, based on parameterized quantum circuits, are universal generative models.
We provide constructive proofs for two extremal circuit designs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Constructive proofs in Section III; summarized in Section VI.

assertions.value: The authors prove necessary conditions on the number of qubits and the number of measurements for expectation value sampling models to be universal, and show a trade-off between the number of measurements and the number of qubits.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, Section I and Section VI
quotes: The second central result is necessary conditions on resources such as the number of qubits and number of measurements for expectation value sampling models to be universal.
we show that there exists a trade-off between the number of measurements and the number of qubits to reach universality.
assertions.certainty_reason: Necessary-condition theorems in Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that stronger advantage arguments for expectation value samplers, in which no polynomial-time randomized Turing machine can sample the output distribution under standard assumptions, are left for future work.
quotes: polynomial-time randomized Turing machine (subject to standard assumptions) but we leave this for future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in Section VI.

papers.title_in_file: Measurement-Based Infused Circuits for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
papers.version_note: The file name carries the arXiv v1 style title (Hybrid variational quantum eigensolvers merging computational models ...); the text inside is v3 titled Measurement-Based Infused Circuits for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers. Same arXiv id 2305.19200.
papers.what_it_is: A VQE method paper that infuses measurement-based ideas into circuit ansatzes and runs demonstrations on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that they perform the first demonstrations of circuit VQEs exploiting MB-VQE ideas on quantum computers (IBM Quantum).
quotes: In particular, we perform the first demonstrations of circuit VQEs exploiting MB-VQE ideas on quantum computers (IBM Quantum).
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority claim by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that a Pauli gadget uses n CZs instead of 2(n − 1) cascaded CXs in the ancilla-free implementation, which they describe as a factor-of-two reduction in entangling gates with constant overhead.
quotes: n CZs instead of the 2(n − 1) cascaded CXs in the
This factor-of-two reduction in entangling gates with constant overhead is relevant for NISQ implementations
assertions.certainty_reason: A gate-count comparison stated in the text, not a theorem.

assertions.value: The authors report that for LiH on ibm_perth the VQE converges within 1.1% of the ground-state energy after 99 function evaluations, with fidelity improving from 0.067 to 0.78.
quotes: The progress plots in Fig. 2(e) verify the effective performance of the ansatz, as the VQE converges within 1.1% of
after 99 function evaluations, with F improving from 0.067 to 0.78.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one hardware run.

assertions.value: The authors state that the final error and fidelity of the LiH run contain contributions from hardware noise and from the limitation of a single gadget in capturing all other interaction terms in the Hamiltonian.
quotes: contain contributions from not only hardware noise, but also the limitation of a single gadget in capturing all other interaction terms in the Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in the quantum chemistry paragraph.

papers.title_in_file: Tutorial: Calibration refinement in quantum annealing
papers.what_it_is: A D-Wave tutorial on shimming, a calibration refinement method for quantum annealers, with worked examples and code.

assertions.value: The authors define shimming as inferring statistical features of an ideal annealer and tuning the Hamiltonian to produce these features.
quotes: inferring statistical features of an ideal annealer, and tuning the Hamiltonian to produce these features.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of its term, Part I.B.

assertions.value: The authors state that shimming methods should be applied to any detailed study of quantum systems in a quantum annealer and will generally provide a significant improvement to the results.
quotes: These methods should be applied to any detailed study of quantum systems in a quantum annealer, and will generally provide a significant improvement to the results.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing the benefit of its own method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the examples are written for use in an Advantage processor but are not specific to that model, or even to D-Wave quantum annealers in general.
quotes: The examples in this document are written for use in an Advantage processor, but are not specific to that model,
or even to D-Wave quantum annealers in general.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Part VII.

assertions.value: The authors report for the triangular antiferromagnet experiment that shimming improves statistical homogeneity of magnetizations and frustration, with no appreciable impact on the average magnitude of the order parameter.
quotes: shimming improves statistical homogeneity of magnetizations and frustration.
is no appreciable impact on the average magnitude of the order parameter
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment by the device vendor.

papers.title_in_file: QPanda: high-performance quantum computing framework for multiple application scenarios
papers.what_it_is: A vendor paper (Origin Quantum) that presents the QPanda quantum programming framework and benchmarks it against other libraries.

assertions.value: The authors state that QPanda is an application scenario-oriented quantum programming framework with high-performance simulation, and that it supports research in quantum finance, quantum chemistry, and quantum fluid mechanics.
quotes: this paper proposes QPanda, an application scenario-oriented quantum programming framework with high-performance simulation.
supports the research of quantum finance, quantum chemistry, quantum fluid mechanics, etc.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describing its own product.

assertions.value: The authors state that the CPU and GPU benchmarks prove the high performance of QPanda simulation and that its performance is top of the compared libraries.
quotes: the CPU and GPU benchmarks prove the high performance of QPanda simulation, and the performance is top of compared libs.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company's benchmark of its own product; figures are in Figs. 10-12, not in the quotes.

assertions.value: The authors report that the compared libraries have similar CPU performance after 20 qubits without optimizing, and that QPanda has the best performance when its optimizing option is open.
quotes: whole lib's benchmarks have similar performance after 20 qubits without optimizing.
However, QPanda has the best performance when opening the optimizing option
assertions.certainty_reason: A company's benchmark of its own product.

assertions.value: The authors state that after mapping on cycle or grid topology, the optimized circuit depth and CNOT numbers are shorter than the pre-optimizing result.
quotes: We can see that the optimized result's circuit depth and CNOT numbers are shorter than the pre-optimizing result.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company's result on its own product; the figures are in Table 3, not in the quote.

papers.title_in_file: Optimizing Machine Learning Potentials for Hydroxide Transport: Surprising Efficiency of Single-Concentration Training
papers.what_it_is: A classical machine learning study of how fine-tuned MACE interatomic potentials transfer across KOH concentrations.

assertions.value: The authors report that models fine-tuned on specific KOH concentrations exhibit surprisingly poor transferability to others, with force prediction errors increasing dramatically from 30 meV (per angstrom) at the training concentration to a much higher error at very different concentrations.
quotes: models fine-tuned on specific KOH concentrations exhibit surprisingly poor transferability to others, with force prediction errors increasing dramatically from 30 meV
This reveals a critical limitation when applying such models beyond their training domain, even within chemically homogeneous systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the 90 meV figure is in the abstract but not quoted.

assertions.value: The authors report that models fine-tuned on intermediate concentrations (particularly at 6.26 mol L−1) exhibit transferability across the entire concentration range and often outperform multi-concentration models, and that the single-concentration model trained on 6.26 mol L−1 outperforms most combined-dataset models.
quotes: First, models fine-tuned on intermediate concentrations (particularly at 6.26 mol L−1) exhibit exceptional transferability across the entire concentration range, often outperforming more complex multi-concentration models
Remarkably, the single-concentration model trained on 6.26 mol L−1 outperforms most of the more computationally intensive combined-dataset models.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study of one material system.

assertions.value: The authors state that a well-chosen single-concentration model can be as effective as sophisticated multi-concentration models when the target concentration range is known, and that for highly variable concentrations the combined-dataset models (B2 and B3) may justify their higher computational cost.
quotes: This suggests that a well-chosen single-concentration model can be as effective as sophisticated multi-concentration models, particularly when the target concentration range is known.
For systems with highly variable concentrations, the combined-dataset models (B2 and B3) may justify their higher computational cost
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' interpretation of their own results.

assertions.value: The authors report that models fine-tuned on dilute solutions significantly underestimate hydroxide jumps at higher concentrations (by up to 45 %), while models trained on concentrated solutions overestimate jumps at lower concentrations (by about 15 %).
quotes: Models fine-tuned on dilute solutions significantly underestimate hydroxide jumps at higher concentrations (by up to 45 %), while models trained on concentrated solutions overestimate jumps at lower concentrations (by about 15 %).
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

papers.title_in_file: VQE-generated quantum circuit dataset for machine learning
papers.what_it_is: A dataset paper that proposes clustering and classification of VQE-optimized quantum circuits as a quantum machine learning task.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dataset uses six common types of Hamiltonians in condensed matter physics with a range of 4-20 qubits and ten different ansatz with varying depths (ranging from 3 to 32), giving a dataset of six distinct classes each containing 300 samples.
quotes: We utilized six common types of Hamiltonians in condensed matter physics, with a range of 4-20 qubits, and applied ten different ansatz with varying depths (ranging from 3 to 32) to generate a quantum circuit dataset of six distinct classes, each containing 300 samples.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report that with clustering based on the exact fidelity-based distance for ideal quantum computers, the adjusted Rand index for the 4-, 8-, 12-, 16- and 20-qubit datasets is respectively 0.992, 0.968, 0.927, 0.883 and 0.692.
quotes: To demonstrate the ease of clustering the proposed dataset for ideal quantum computers, we perform clustering based on the exact value of dij.
The ARI of the 4-, 8-, 12-, 16- and 20-qubit dataset is respectively 0.992, 0.968, 0.927, 0.883 and 0.692.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study under ideal (exact-value) conditions.

assertions.value: The authors report perfect clustering of the four-qubit subdataset using fidelities measured on the ibmq manila device, and an ARI of 0.720 for the dataset of 20 qubits on FakeAuckland, a simulator mimicking an IBM device.
quotes: As we can observe, we are able to perfectly cluster the dataset.
The ARI is 0.720. This indicates the possibility of learning our dataset using real devices even at the size of 20 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the 20-qubit result is a noise-model simulation, not hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report classification accuracy of up to about 80% for the Hamiltonian ansatz, and state that classification models such as SVM do not work well on the proposed dataset even for the very simplified task.
quotes: For Hamiltonian ansatz, we reached a higher classification accuracy of up to about 80% than other
classification models such as SVM do not work well on the proposed dataset even for the very simplified task.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
